title: Equidimensionality after polynomial extension and localization
statement: Let $(C,\mathfrak n)$ be a Noetherian local ring such that $\operatorname{Spec}(C)$ is equidimensional, and let $\mathfrak n'\subset C[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ be a maximal ideal lying over $\mathfrak n$. If $C$ is complete, then $C[x_1,\ldots,x_r]_{\mathfrak n'}$ is catenary and its spectrum is equidimensional; every irreducible component has dimension $\dim C+r$. [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] [def-weil-affine-spectrum] [def-weil-irreducible-components] [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] [def-exc-excellent-ring] [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]

source.place: Tag 0AW5, lemma-formally-catenary, proof paragraph after the completion-flat map: polynomial completion is catenary and minimal components have dimension dim(C)+r

proof.text: Put $P=C[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$, $S=P\setminus\mathfrak n'$ and $D=S^{-1}P$. The polynomial algebra $P$ is finite type over the Noetherian ring $C$, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes $P$ Noetherian. Every ideal $J\subset D$ is extended from its contraction $I\subset P$: if $a/s\in J$, then $a/1=(s/1)(a/s)\in J$, so $a\in I$, and the opposite inclusion follows by multiplying by $1/s$. Images of finitely many generators of $I$ generate $J$. Thus $D$ is Noetherian, and [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] makes it local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n'D$.

source.place: Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence; localization argument written out, and Tag 00CO, definition-localization

proof.text: The completeness hypothesis is completeness for the maximal-ideal topology. Apply [lem-per-complete-local-excellence] to the given Noetherian local ring $C$. By [def-exc-excellent-ring], excellence implies universal catenarity, so the finite type $C$-algebra $P$ is catenary. To pass to $D$, primes correspond by extension and contraction to primes of $P$ contained in $\mathfrak n'$: the inverse to contraction sends $Q$ to the fractions with numerator in $Q$. Between two such primes every intermediate prime is still contained in $\mathfrak n'$. Thus their entire intervals, strict inclusions and saturated chains agree with those in $D$. The finite chain bound and equality of saturated lengths for $P$ therefore hold for $D$. Hence $D$ is catenary.

source.place: Tag 0AW5, lemma-formally-catenary, catenarity paragraph; complete-local excellence is Tag 07QW, proposition-ubiquity-excellent (2), and localization uses the prime-interval argument of algebra.tex Tag 00NJ, lemma-localization-catenary

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak q$ be any minimal prime of $D$, and let $Q$ be its contraction to $P$. By [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime], choose a minimal prime $\mathfrak p$ of $C$ contained in $Q\cap C$. Coefficient reduction $P\to(C/\mathfrak p)[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ is onto with kernel $\mathfrak pP$: a polynomial is in the kernel exactly when all its finitely many coefficients lie in $\mathfrak p$. The quotient is a domain: order monomials lexicographically; the largest monomial of a product of two nonzero polynomials is the product of their largest monomials and has nonzero coefficient. Thus $\mathfrak pP$ is prime. Since $\mathfrak pP\subset Q\subset\mathfrak n'$, it is disjoint from $S$ and its extension $\mathfrak pD$ is a proper prime contained in $\mathfrak q$. Minimality gives $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak pD$. This supplies the source's omitted minimal-prime argument using only prime existence and the coefficient and fraction definitions [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

source.place: Tag 0AW5, lemma-formally-catenary, sentence identifying each minimal prime as an extended minimal prime (small detail omitted in the source)

proof.text:
Fix the $\mathfrak p$ from Step 3 and put $R=C/\mathfrak p$, $T=R[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak n/\mathfrak p$, and $M=\mathfrak n'/\mathfrak pP\subset T$. Then $R$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and $M$ is maximal with contraction $\mathfrak m$, since $T/M=P/\mathfrak n'$ is a field. Both $R$ and $T$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], applied first to the quotient $C\to R$ and then to its polynomial algebra. Coefficient reduction and fractions give
$$D/\mathfrak q\ \cong\ T_M,\qquad (f/s)\bmod\mathfrak q\longmapsto\bar f/\bar s.$$
Every denominator of $T\setminus M$ lifts to one of $P\setminus\mathfrak n'$, so the map is onto; it kills precisely those fractions with some $S$-multiple of their numerator in $\mathfrak pP$, which is exactly the extended ideal $\mathfrak pD=\mathfrak q$. This verifies the identification directly [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

source.place: Tag 0AW5, lemma-formally-catenary, minimal-component quotient in the last displayed dimension calculation; coefficient/fraction calculation written out

proof.text:
The map $R\to T$ is flat directly from [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and the monomial description [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. For any $R$-module $N$, the map
$$N\otimes_R T\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\mathbf N^r}N,\qquad n\otimes\sum_\alpha a_\alpha x^\alpha\longmapsto(a_\alpha n)_\alpha$$
has inverse $(n_\alpha)_\alpha\mapsto\sum_\alpha n_\alpha\otimes x^\alpha$. The sums are finite and these maps are inverse by tensor bilinearity. Tensoring an injective map $N_1\to N_2$ with $T$ consequently applies that injective map separately to each coefficient, so stays injective. This is precisely the cited definition of flatness, rather than an uncited appeal to free modules being flat.

source.place: Tag 00HB, definition-flat; elementary monomial tensor calculation for the polynomial map used in Tag 0AW5

proof.text:
Put $k=R/\mathfrak m=C/\mathfrak n$ and $M_0=M/\mathfrak mT\subset k[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$. This is maximal because $\mathfrak mT\subset M$ and its quotient is the field $T/M$. Reducing coefficients in fractions gives
$$T_M/\mathfrak mT_M\ \cong\ k[x_1,\ldots,x_r]_{M_0}.$$
Indeed every polynomial outside $M_0$ lifts to one outside $M$; the kernel consists of fractions having a denominator-complement multiple of the numerator in $\mathfrak mT$, exactly $\mathfrak mT_M$, by the fraction equality in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-maximal-localization-dimension] to the field $k$, the nonnegative integer $r$, and its maximal ideal $M_0$. The dimension of this closed-fibre local ring is therefore $r$; no rationality assumption on the closed point is needed.

source.place: Tag 00OP, lemma-dim-affine-space, dimension of polynomial localization at any maximal ideal; coefficient/fraction identification in Tag 0AW5

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula] to the flat map $R\to T$ of Noetherian rings and the prime $M$ contracting to $\mathfrak m$. All these hypotheses were checked in Steps 4 and 5. Its local dimension equality yields
$$\dim T_M=\dim R_{\mathfrak m}+\dim(T_M/\mathfrak mT_M)=\dim R+r.$$
Here $R_{\mathfrak m}=R$ since $R$ is local (every denominator outside its maximal ideal is already a unit), and Step 6 supplies the second summand. Step 4 now gives $\dim(D/\mathfrak q)=\dim(C/\mathfrak p)+r$.

source.place: Tag 00ON, lemma-dimension-base-fibre-equals-total, applied to a polynomial algebra; this is the first equality of the final display in more-algebra.tex Tag 0AW5

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes], $V(\mathfrak p)$ is an irreducible component of $\operatorname{Spec}C$. Primes of $C/\mathfrak p$ are exactly primes of $C$ containing $\mathfrak p$, with the same closed subsets $V(I)$; hence $\operatorname{Spec}(C/\mathfrak p)$ identifies with $V(\mathfrak p)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-topological-krull-dimension-ring] its dimension is $\dim(C/\mathfrak p)$. Equidimensionality of $\operatorname{Spec}C$ makes this value independent of $\mathfrak p$ and equal to $\dim C$: every chain of primes lies above a minimal prime contained in its smallest member, by [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime], so the supremum of component dimensions is the dimension of the whole spectrum. The same component correspondence for $D$ identifies every irreducible component with $\operatorname{Spec}(D/\mathfrak q)$ for some minimal $\mathfrak q$. Step 7 and the arbitrary choice of $\mathfrak q$ give dimension $\dim C+r$ for every one. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}D$ is equidimensional, completing the conclusion together with Step 2.

source.place: Tag 0AW5, lemma-formally-catenary, second equality of final display and conclusion; component correspondence is algebra.tex Tag 00ES, lemma-irreducible, and dimension is Tag 00KE, definition-Krull
